title: I was eviscerated for posting this in Play My Game
author: Unique-Phone-1087
selftext:
Be honest with me, would you call this AI Slop?

I would explain what went into developing this, but I don't want to prejudice your answer.

The game is a colony sim with lane-defender combat for mobile. You can play it in browser at [https://dashiellrenaud.com/abomination](https://dashiellrenaud.com/abomination)

Happy to send the iOS or Android version to anyone who wants it.

comments.author: macronancer
comments.body:
Dont listen to the morons in here that have never created a thing in their life.

Keep going, you are soing great! Keep iterating and playing your game. Always ask yourself: what is the fun factor, is this fun to play *for me*?

Focus on gameplay, use polygon assets, you can always change the graphics later, focus on the core mechanics.

replies.author: Unique-Phone-1087
replies.body:
That’s very kind of you to say! I really appreciate their feedback though. And this is the point where I need to start thinking about how everything looks and feels in the eyes of others.

The mini game estate map, for example, which two commenters here have seized upon, actually represents a huge amount of hand-made art and effort on my part. I was so proud to make something that looks (imho) much better than Travian, and which has been entirely populated with constructable and destructible elements. But if it looks like AI-ass though, it’s clearly gotta go.

A good rule to follow is that if any of your art looks like obvious AI art to people then it's not good enough.

Think of it like CG in movies, when it's invisible or extremely well done nobody cares, as soon as it sticks out or looks sloppy everyone becomes a CG hater.

comments.author: Bratchan
comments.body:
Yes  
You have super AI front screen, then map.. and then the really bad generic HML generated characters.. the ui in game is just bad..  

AI is a tool to speed up things so you can FINE tune the rest which you did not 

If you want the more hand draw bad style your hole game needs to reflect it. You need to understand  AI and then simple Art  clashes hard. you got to take the time to make assets, UI etc to match.  If this was just you saying hey testing game mechanics Ok this would be fine.. but not this is your calling it a finished game. 

its hard to know which one is you vs everyone else. you got to make your main character stand out. Use the anime joke, which one is the main character cause they stand out like a sore thumb usally. 

So take the time.. figure out what you want this game to look like. Then slowly learn how to make all the assets look the same. You can also use Photopea (Free photoshop)  they also have an illustrator version now if you want SVGs.

This has been very helpful though for the purpose of understanding that the wrong aesthetics will prevent anyone from looking into the mechanics.

replies.author: Atmic
replies.body:
Always be careful sharing unfinished/unpolished material to the world.

As soon as it's in the public you're opening yourself up to criticism at the highest level.   
  
You want to make sure your stuff is the very best you can polish it before dropping it in the shark tank.

comments.author: DerelictCoffee
comments.body: Listen some people just want to shit all over anything and everything associated with AI. It is what it is and it's more so to do with the failure of big tech to properly steward this new tech than those of us who are early to adopt it.  Your game doesn't look like slop, but it does look like someone learning.  That's ok.  You need help with style, structure and art direction and that's ok. The whole point of AI is that it allows you to improve the baseline where you lack skills.  Keep going, don't get discouraged and work on learning to use style sheets, art direction and strict art prompting with your tools.  Your art isn't awful btw, just not professional.  And I say that as someone learning too, my game has issues too. 100% but at the end of the day I'm having a good time making it and learning as I go. That's job #1. This is my project if you want to compare art direction. [https://derelique.itch.io/trueofvoice](https://derelique.itch.io/trueofvoice)

comments.author: ffxivthrowaway03
comments.body:
I wouldn't use the word "slop" given it's loaded context, but yeah.  The visual style is all over the place, the UI/UX is extremely barebones and *full* of errors, there's no real identity, it's a mess top to bottom. This is a rudimentary concept prototype, not a game.

And the title "Abomination - An experiment in galvanism" is off-putting and comes off as "Iamverysmart" - This game isn't a philosophical stroll through an interesting concept, it's a lane battler with a bunch of little stick figure dudes shooting at each other.  My very first question was "what the fuck does any of this have to do with anything, much less galvanism?"  Beyond a vague reference to Frankenstein's monster on the character selector, the answer is *nothing*.

replies.author: Unique-Phone-1087
replies.body:
Well, one piece of the art is actually a famous 19th century painting. 

A lot of this is placeholder, but a solid day of work went into the estate screen that various people have complained about. It started as a crude hand drawing and I was initially impressed with what I was able to get from the hand drawn image. And a good amount of work went into making each plot on the map a place that can be developed or destroyed, and showing each piece in different states. Clearly that’s all a wash. 

Some of the animations are entirely first-draft, and I think it’s easy to lose sight of that after looking at things for a while. The points about visual inconsistency and overall blandness are very well taken.

But I kind of assumed that people would surmise that this is an AI game with placeholder art and actually maybe take a stab at evaluating it mechanically (my mistake; also a very good lesson!)

What’s shown in the video here is just a mini game and a glimpse of the combat system. 

If you take the mechanics for a spin and still come away with the sense that this is single-prompt slop, then I indeed have wasted considerable time and energy on garbage.

comments.author: AshinaBeats
comments.body:
it's not AI slop. It seems like you put a decent amount of thought and work from the setup screen to the main gameplay.

As others say, the aesthetic is very off though. You start with a dark medieval atmosphere in the beginning, then show the cartoon south park-style characters, then the map is a nice hand-drawn style. I think these aesthetics problems are the reason why people might call your game "slop".

Aesthetic style is very,very important for a game. It's a game and not a tool after all. Try to work on having a consistent art style, whether you want to copy a style from an existing game, use AI-generated art, whatever path you want to take. But you should do it at this stage in your project rather than later, because it's much harder to fix later + a lot of people whom you show it to will give you negative feedback around the art style, so better to resolve that first.

Good luck

replies.author: Unique-Phone-1087
replies.body:
Thank you for the thoughtful feedback! Most appreciated.

I’m definitely going to make sure the graphics and video are a lot more polished before I come back around looking for feedback 😅

This has been a helpful and humbling experience!

replies.author: AshinaBeats
replies.body: no problem! just adding a trivial comment: if this was normal software, i would work in the opposite order, of having NO design and keeping things completely bare bones, and just focus on the function/mechanics. But for a game I think getting the art style and the atmosphere and vision first is better. Good games have a distinct style/atmosphere, and it soaks into each flavor text, each dialog, even setting screens.
